title: Lavender & kaolin clay bar soap
subtitle: A pale grey-white bar for all skin types
excerpt: Cold-process bar soap with fine white kaolin clay for a slight draw and silky feel, scented with lavender essential oil. Made on coconut, olive, and castor oil at a 5% superfat. The clay gives the lather a smooth, velvety quality. Yields eight bars; hardens in 4-6 weeks.
sourceNotes: Susan Miller Cavitch, The Soapmaker's Companion (1997), clay in cold-process soap: usage rate 1 teaspoon per 450 g oil; incorporated at trace as part of the fragrance addition. Kaolin clay: the mildest cosmetic clay; fine white particles; does not draw as strongly as bentonite. Lavender EO in CP soap: stable at trace up to 3% of oil weight. Soap-Calc SAP values (accessed 2026): coconut 0.190, olive 0.134, castor 0.128.

recipe.batchNotes: Kaolin clay absorbs oils and can thicken the batter more quickly than expected. Disperse it in a tablespoon of the recipe's oil before adding to the batter at trace to distribute evenly.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bars cure in 4-6 weeks and keep up to 2 years. Lavender EO holds well in cold-process soap and the scent remains good for the full shelf life.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 2 years in a cool, dry place. Lavender is one of the most stable essential oils in cold-process soap. Discard at any sign of orange spots (DOS) on the cut face or a rancid smell.

glossaryTerms.definition: The reaction between fat and sodium hydroxide that produces soap. Kaolin clay does not participate in saponification; it's an additive added at trace after the reaction is underway.
The point at which the blended soap batter thickens enough to hold a faint drizzled trail, when additives like clay and essential oils are stirred in and the batter is ready to mould.
The percentage of oil left unsaponified in the finished bar, contributing conditioning properties. This recipe uses 5%.

content.text: Lavender and kaolin clay soap is a pale, fine-grained cold-process bar with a silky, velvety lather. Fine white kaolin clay, the mildest of the cosmetic clays, gives a slight drawing quality without the sharp pulling of stronger clays like bentonite. Lavender essential oil scents the bar and holds well through the cure. Made on coconut, olive, and castor oil at a 5% superfat. Eight bars; hardens in 4-6 weeks.
Ingredients

items.prepNote: pure (not extra virgin); 45% of oil weight; conditioning base
40% of oil weight; lather and hardness
15% of oil weight; high castor for conditioning, stabilises lather
NaOH at 99% purity; calculated for 5% superfat
32% of oil weight; the lye solution liquid
3% of oil weight; stir in at trace, not blended in
white kaolin clay; disperse in 1 tbsp olive oil before adding to batter at trace

content.text: Method
Make the lye solution
Put on protective gloves and goggles. Work in a ventilated space. Pour the sodium hydroxide slowly into the distilled water in the HDPE pitcher, stirring until dissolved. Cool to 38-42°C.
Disperse the clay
Mix the kaolin clay into 1 tablespoon of olive oil (taken from the recipe weight) until a smooth paste forms with no dry lumps. Set aside.
Prepare the oils and blend to trace
Melt the coconut oil, combine with the remaining olive oil and castor oil, and bring to 38-42°C.
Pour the lye solution into the oils. Stick-blend in short bursts until light
trace
Stir in the clay paste and the lavender essential oil by hand. Mix until evenly distributed.
Pour into the mould, insulate with a towel, and leave 24-48 hours. Unmould when firm, cut into 8 bars wearing gloves, and cure on a ventilated rack for 4-6 weeks.
The
saponification
is complete when a corner touched to the tongue gives no zap. The finished bars are white to pale grey with a smooth, even texture.
Storage and shelf life
Store cured bars on a ventilated rack in a cool, dry cupboard. Lavender essential oil is one of the most stable EOs in soap, the scent holds for the full 2-year shelf life. The
superfat
from the castor and olive oils keeps the bar conditioning throughout. Discard at any sign of orange spots (DOS) or rancid smell.
